title: From AGI to ASI: Four Pathways to Superintelligence
hook: A DeepMind team maps four routes from human-level AGI to superintelligence - and argues the leap may arrive as a series of transformative shifts, not one dramatic step change.
key_points: Frames machine intelligence as a continuum from AGI toward Universal AI, whose endpoint is theoretically well understood.
Defines ASI as a system more cognitively capable than large organizations of humans.
Proposes four AGI-to-ASI pathways: scaling AGI, AI paradigm shifts, recursive self-improvement, and emergence from large-scale multi-agent collectives.
Stresses that frictions and bottlenecks along each path determine whether progress stalls or accelerates.
Argues the future may be many transformative changes across science and technology, not a single AGI step change.
content_html: For most of the last decade, human-level AGI sat in the realm of speculation. This report, from a group of DeepMind researchers (including Shane Legg and Marcus Hutter), treats it instead as a concrete next-decade target and asks the follow-up question: what happens after? It frames machine intelligence as a continuum stretching from AGI toward Universal AI — an endpoint that is, the authors note, theoretically well understood — and focuses on the transition to artificial superintelligence (ASI), a system more capable than large organizations of humans.
extra_html: The report lays out four candidate pathways from AGI to ASI: scaling AGI further, AI paradigm shifts, recursive self-improvement, and ASI emerging from large-scale multi-agent collectives. For each, it weighs the frictions and bottlenecks that could either stall progress or prove negligible. A central argument: the popular image of one transformative step change when AGI arrives may be misleading. More apt, the authors suggest, is a series of transformative changes rippling across science and technology — which is why they call for a broad, interdisciplinary effort to prepare. This is a position and analysis piece; its pathways and claims are the authors' framing, not settled results.

related.title: On the Measure of Intelligence (ARC)
related.hook: Is a high benchmark score the same as intelligence? Chollet argues no — intelligence is how efficiently you acquire new skills, not how well you perform known ones.

related.title: Model Evaluation for Extreme Risks
related.hook: General-purpose AI tends to pick up dangerous capabilities alongside useful ones. So test for those capabilities directly — before you ship, not after.

related.title: Frontier AI Regulation
related.hook: How do you regulate models too new to have rules yet? This paper sketches three building blocks: set standards, make labs report, then enforce.

flashcards.prompt: How does the report define ASI (artificial superintelligence)?
flashcards.back_html: A system more intelligent and cognitively capable than large organizations of humans — a point further along the machine-intelligence continuum than human-level AGI.

flashcards.prompt: Which is one of the four AGI-to-ASI pathways the report proposes?

choices.text: ASI emerging from large-scale multi-agent collectives
Banning all frontier training runs worldwide

flashcards.explanation_html: The four pathways are scaling AGI, AI paradigm shifts, recursive self-improvement, and emergence from large-scale multi-agent collectives.

flashcards.prompt: What's the report's view on whether AGI causes a single 'step change'?
flashcards.back_html: Probably not — it may instead be a series of transformative societal changes driven by AI-enabled breakthroughs across many areas of science and technology.
